c. Traffic Noise:
(1) Projected Traffic: An examination of the highway noise exposure of the Randolph Urban Renewal Area reveals that the proposed Downtown Expressway will be the major noise factor within the project area. The 1985 average traffic volume for the arterial is projected at 56,000 vehicles, with a design hour volume of approximately 5,200 vehicles (two-way). The percentage of trucks is expected to be less than five percent.
The traffic speeds used in the noise calculations were based on all vehicles stopping at the Lombardy Street toll booth, decelerating from 50-60 mph and then accelerating back to 50-60 mph. Highway grades at either side of the toll booth are of particular significance in determing truck speed as a function of distance from the toll gate, since the uphill grade will strongly affect the time and distance required for a truck to achieve highway speed. Proposed roadway gradients were supplied by Richmond Metropolitan Authority.
(2) Noise Evaluation Study: A detailed noise evaluation study was conducted by Bolt, Beranek and Newman, Inc. (Cambridge, Massachusetts), one of the leading consultants in the field. Using specialized computer programs, the firm has drawn noise level contours for areas adjacent to the expressway. Attenuation measures were then designed capable of reducing noise exposure levels within residential areas to acceptable levels according to HUD criteria. The firm's recommendations have been included as part of the renewal plans for Randolph.
